today.name: Glasshand
today.tagline: Give your agent a real iPhone and Mac
today.description: Glasshand gives your AI agents real iPhones and Macs to work on. Connect Claude Code, Codex, or any other agent, and it can rent a device with a single prompt. The hardware sits in our data center, and your agent uses it the way you would: posting on TikTok, booking an Uber, or building and testing iOS apps. Each device is yours alone for as long as you rent it. When you’re done, we erase your data and factory-reset it.

comments.text: Hey everyone. I’m Trevor, creator of Glasshand.We’re the team behind Solid, from MIT, Berkeley, and Waterloo. We’ve raised $6M to build toward one goal: agents with human-level autonomy.Agents are already smart enough for most of what you’d ask them to do, but a simple task on a phone can still leave yours waiting for you to open an app and tap a few buttons.So we built Glasshand to give your agent hands of its own: real iPhones and Macs in our data center, not emulators or virtual machines. Now your agent can use Apple apps and services, including iCloud.That puts your agent inside the Apple ecosystem, with access to Apple’s apps and services. It can develop iOS apps on a Mac and test them on a physical iPhone, book rides on Uber, post on TikTok and Instagram, or sign in to your iCloud account and use it the way you would.Because these are real iPhones, you can even add an eSIM plan with SMS and mobile data. That gives your agent its own phone number and cellular connection, so it can get verification codes on its iPhone without waiting for you to pass them along.Glasshand works with any agent. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or whatever you already use can rent an iPhone and a Mac from our platform through our API.Each device starts clean and is only yours for the length of your subscription. You set the password yourself, and we can’t see it. When you’re done, we erase your data and factory-reset the device.Happy to answer any questions here.

Real device control is huge for agents - but latency spikes on network hiccups could kill agentic workflows. How do you handle timeout recovery without breaking the session state? That's your real differentiator.

Real devices instead of emulators is a big deal. As a front-end dev, half my “works on my machine” bugs only show up in Safari on an actual iPhone. Could an agent use Glasshand to open a staging URL in mobile Safari, run through a flow, and report back with screenshots? That would be a huge time saver for mobile web QA. Congrats on the launch!

Using real devices makes sense here—iCloud authentication and SMS verification are often where agent workflows get stuck. When an agent signs into iCloud on a freshly reset iPhone, how do you manage Apple’s 2FA checks and approval prompts on trusted devices?

Real hardware instead of a simulator is the right call for anything touching iCloud sign-in or SMS codes, which is exactly where agent flows usually stall. How do you handle Apple's 2FA and trusted-device prompts when an agent signs into iCloud on a freshly reset phone?
We had to open a TikTok account with a real phone number last week, so real devices make sense to me. Does a rented iPhone keep the same number between rentals?

Real devices make sense for apps that fingerprint emulators, but I wonder about the other side. TikTok and Instagram are pretty aggressive about flagging automated behavior, so does an agent tapping around from a data center IP on a rented SE put the user's account at risk? Curious if you have seen bans or step-up verification during testing.
@tkeith i love this. I'm currently piecing together a bunch of old machines, but this would be a much better solution. I look forward to checking it out.

today.name: Rerun
today.tagline: Turn your AI subscriptions into a team of coworkers
today.description: Rerun turns your ChatGPT or Claude subscription into a team of AI coworkers. Each one has tools, a computer and a shared workspace, runs on a schedule or a trigger, and asks before risky actions. Now open-source (AGPL v3) and self-hostable.
today.category: Productivity • Open Source • Artificial Intelligence • GitHub

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋I'm Clément, and with Théo we build Rerun: AI coworkers that actually do the work. Each one gets its own tools, its own computer (a real browser you can watch and take over), a memory and a schedule. They chase invoices, qualify leads and sort your inbox, and they stop and ask before they send, pay or delete anything.Today Rerun goes open source under AGPL-3.0. I've been a developer for 15 years, and almost everything I've built stands on open source. Giving back felt obvious, and Rerun is the most complete product we've ever built, so it's the right one to share.Clone the repo, run docker compose up, and your coworkers run on your own server, on the Claude or ChatGPT plan you already pay for, or any model through OpenRouter. If you'd rather not run anything, Rerun Cloud is the same code, ready in 30 seconds.

Orchestrating across subscriptions requires robust state machines - one API timeout cascades the whole workflow. How do you handle partial failures and recovery without losing context? That's what separates reliable agents from brittle workflows.

congrats on the launch clement. asking before a risky step is the part that makes me trust a coworker agent. soft wording on the prompt is what burned me before, so i hope it shows the exact action not only a nice summary
For invoice chasing, can it check whether a payment arrived before sending the next reminder? That would be my first workflow to try.
I’d start with sorting emails and drafting replies. The pause before sending would make that a much easier first step.

Open sourcing under AGPL is a bold call for something that runs on people's own ChatGPT/Claude subscriptions. When an agent asks for approval before a risky action, does it show the exact payload it is about to send (the email body, the amount), or just a summary of the intent?

today.name: Living Brain
today.tagline: Interoperable, efficient memory layer for agentic AI
today.description: Every AI conversation contains knowledge worth keeping, but most of it gets trapped in separate chats and tools. Living Brain captures that knowledge, connects it to what you already know, and turns it into a persistent memory that keeps evolving. Share that intelligence across AI models, apps, and agents through API, SDK, or MCP, so every new interaction builds on the last instead of starting over. Reuse memory across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, OpenClaw, Hermes, Cursor, Codex and more

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I’m Christel, founder of ChatAndBuild, and I was part of Twitter's first international team.We have built the Living Brain - a model independent, harness independent, efficient brain that travels with you across any AI platform.Living Brain gives your AI tools a shared, persistent memory. It turns your notes, documents and conversations into connected knowledge that you can inspect, update and reuse across compatible assistants and agents.For example, save a project brief, customer requirements and the decisions behind your roadmap in one brain. Connect it to your AI tools, and they can retrieve that context when you ask them to work on the project.With Living Brain, you can:🧠 Build a memory around your work, projects and preferences.🔗 Reuse that memory across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, OpenClaw, Hermes, Cursor, Codex and more🛠️ Give your own apps and agents persistent context through our API.📚 Review the organised knowledge and the sources behind it.We’re measuring how accurately AI can use that memory, alongside how much context it needs.Our latest internal evaluations show:We're #1 on LoCoMo with 92.2% judged accuracy, answering 1,420/1,540 questions correctly with approximately 63.8% less context.Those context reductions compare average retrieved memory with the displayed full-history references — approximately 9.4K versus 26K tokens on LoCoMo, and 5.1K versus 115K on LongMemEval-S.We want you to choose each AI for what it does best, with your accumulated context coming along.We’re building this for people who use several AI tools, teams whose context is scattered, and developers building agents that need continuity.I’d love to hear from you. What’s the one thing you’re tired of explaining to AI over and over?Tell us your workflow. I’d love to see where Living Brain could help, and where we still need to improve.— Christel

The Freshness and Strain signals are the part I'd actually use: stale memory quietly beating newer context is the failure I keep running into. When two connected tools write conflicting facts into the same brain, which one wins, and can I see the conflict?

congrats on the launch christel. to your question, which pages actually convert and which just get traffic. agents forget that every session -> if memory also kept why i rejected a draft last week that alone would help
Definitely interesting, would love to test it out, From where to try it?

Living Brain helps to solve a frustration that many of us know firsthand: having to repeat the same context every time we switch AI tools. For me, knowing that I can carry my notes, decisions and project context across compatible tools makes it easier to choose the right AI without starting from scratch, and this is exactly the advantage that Living Brain gives you!You can create a Brain in ChatChat without code, or connect Living Brain to your apps through our API, MCP, SDK and CLI. I’m excited to share what we’ve built and would love to hear how it helps you!

My current workflow is a lot of jumping b/w references, random ideas, feedback, and last-minute changes. Because of Living Brain, I can come back to an idea later w/o losing the thought process that made it click. I get to spend more time actually creating instead of retracing how I got there.

I like this. In my experience the built in AI memories keep the wrong things. They drags the reasoning into the output and forgets the one instruction I actually cared about. Can I see why something was kept or left out of a brain?

We built Living Brain because no one should feel stuck with one AI tool just because all of their context is there.You should be free to try what is new, use what works best, and switch when you need to, without starting from scratch each time.Your memory should be yours, and it should travel with you.

today.name: Maritime
today.tagline: Cloud computers for any AI agent, customized your way
today.description: Maritime gives AI agents their own cloud computers: persistent workspaces, disposable sandboxes, Linux and Windows desktops, and Android phones. Agents can run code, use browsers, and work in apps without APIs, with a human able to take over when needed. Whether you’re building a personal assistant or running thousands of tasks in parallel, Maritime handles the computers so you can focus on what your agent does.

comments.text: Hi hackers! I'm Maria, cofounder of Maritime (YC F26). Before Maritime, I researched AI agents at MIT.Agents need different computers for different jobs: a throwaway sandbox for generated code, a workspace that’s still there next week, hundreds of clean machines for an eval, or a desktop for an app with no API. Sometimes they need Windows or a phone.We built Maritime to put all of these behind one API, on one bill. You can host any kind of agent and customize its environment with the software and tools it needs.Sandboxes start at $0.011/hour for 1 vCPU and 2 GB of memory. Linux desktops are $0.12/hour, Windows desktops are $0.18/hour with the licence included, and Android phones are $0.15/hour. All are billed per second while running.There’s a 7-day free trial with up to $20 of usage.What are you building, and what kind of computer does your agent need?

Variable agent workloads make billing complex - pay-as-you-go is tempting but unpredictable costs kill budgeting. How do you handle reservation optimization vs overprovisioning risk? That's the infrastructure moat.
For the eval case with hundreds of clean machines, how long until they're all up? Per-second billing only helps if startup doesn't eat the first minute of every run.
For the Android phones - can an agent install its own apps on them, or do they come as fixed images?
@maria_gorskikh1 Congratulations on the launch. Is this a B2B product?
Disposable sandboxes and persistent workspaces solve different problems. Making that choice explicit when a job starts would help avoid discovering later that a file needed for the next run is gone.

today.name: Pushary for Teams
today.tagline: See who said yes to your team’s AI agents
today.description: When an AI agent stops to ask permission, Pushary sends the question to the person running it, in their Mac’s notch or on their phone. Lee’s agent asks Lee. Sam’s agent asks Sam. A rule can send a push to your infra repo to your lead instead. Answers from the phone, Mac app and dashboard are saved with a name, so when something breaks, one page shows whose agent asked and who said yes. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Agy and Hermes.

comments.text: Hey PH 👋 Aadil here.Pushary shows your AI agent's permission prompts in your Mac's notch, and on your phone when you're away from it. Today it does that for a whole team.Tom's Cursor asks to push to main. He says yes in his terminal. Twelve minutes later prod is down, and the first question in Slack is "whose agent pushed this?" Nobody else saw the question.When it's just you, you know who said yes. Once two or three people run Claude Code, Codex or Cursor on the same code, nobody does. Each agent asks whoever is at that terminal, and nobody else ever sees the yes.On our July launch, Ridhwik put it best: "If my agent drafts an outbound email, the real approver should sometimes be my marketing director, not whoever paired the phone." Eight of you asked for the same thing. So we built it.With Pushary for Teams:When something breaks, one page shows whose agent asked and who tapped yes. The Friday retro takes one page, not an hour in git log.Then add one rule, like "pushes to infra ask the lead first", and next time the lead gets that question.Every agent asks its own person, in the notch at the Mac and on the phone when they're away. Nobody gets the whole team's questions.No scores, no leaderboard. Everyone sees the same page.Honest bits: If you work alone, Claude Code and Codex already let you approve from your phone for free. Use that. Pushary is for when several people's agents need one record, across vendors.Try it: pushary.com/teamsOne command for each person, then scan a QR code with your phone. $59 a month for 5 people, 3 days free for new workspaces, and PHTEAMS takes a month off.For today: reply with the one command you'd never let an agent run without a second person, and I'll reply with the rule that sends it to them.And if Pushary has helped you before, a one-line review would mean a lot. We have exactly one.I'll be here all day <3

today.name: Clocknext
today.tagline: Pricing and Billing Infrastructure for AI Agents
today.description: Clocknext is a billing and monetization platform for AI-native apps and agents. It’s tailored for AI founders, revenue, and engineering teams, to track AI usage from your product in real time, turn it into billable metrics with flexible pricing plans, and monitor costs, margins, and profitability at every level.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋I’m Vijay, founder of @Clocknext. I’ve spent 16 years in software, and for most of that time, “how do you charge?” had a short answer: one-time payments, per seat, per month.AI products changed that. The cost of serving a customer moves with every request, and the unit of value can be credits, outcomes, something you invent, or a mix of all of it.Most teams try out leading billing tools like Stripe, Chargebee, Zuora, etc., and try to make it work for their pricing models, find them lacking, and end up their own billing system: a signals table in Postgres, a cron job that totals the month, and a spreadsheet that matches provider invoices against customer invoices.It holds well at the start. But the problems start when:Pricing needs to change but is waiting on engineering bandwidthYou build new features that require new pricing models that need to be builtRevenue teams lose sight of P&L per customer until it’s too lateWe built Clocknext so you can price an AI product without maintaining that system yourself. With it, you can:Mix credits, outcomes, units, and wallets in one planBill prepaid and postpaid entitlements side by sideSee provider cost next to price, per customer, per agent, and per model🎁 Launch offer: 60% off the annual plan for Product Hunt signups.How are you pricing your agent today? I’ll be in the comments all day.

today.name: Bridge
today.tagline: Video conferencing for the agentic era
today.description: This launch marks a new era for Bridge: one agentic meeting platform replacing the fragmented meeting stack. Bridge now brings scheduling pages, automatic preparation, video conferencing, live intelligence, AI notetaking, agentic workflows, and structured memory into one connected experience for people and agents. At the center of this launch is a new kind of video conferencing built for customizable AI agents to join and participant in meetings.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋Jimmy here, founder of Bridge. Today marks the start of a new chapter.For the past year, we've been building Simplora to help professionals prepare for meetings, get real-time intelligence during meetings, and turn conversations into notes.At the same time, a second pattern was emerging in how our users worked.. they were increasingly turning to AI agents to think and get work done.So we reached a simple conclusion: as AI changes how we work, the way we meet has to evolve just as quickly.But when we looked at the market, we saw:Legacy conferencing platforms adding AI around the edges instead of building for the agentic eraStandalone meeting tools bolted onto platforms where the conversations were already happeningA market split across video conferencing, notetaking, preparation, scheduling, and agentsSo, we decided to build what the market was missing, and to reorient our company around this vision.Today, I’m honored to introduce Bridge: the workspace where teams and agents meet.This launch brings many new product updates, but we’re most proud to announce that we have consolidated the legacy, fragmented meeting stack into one modern agentic platform.Bridge now brings scheduling pages, automatic preparation, video conferencing, live intelligence, AI notetaking, agentic workflows, and structured memory into one connected experience for people and agents.With this launch, we’re also introducing video conferencing for agents.Our proprietary video conferencing infrastructure is designed for customizable AI agents to join and participate in meetings, or work privately in real-time.Not convinced? today.name: Tao Browser
today.tagline: Private browser with a separate login for every company
today.description: Tao Browser keeps each company, client or project in its own space with its own cookies and logins. Lock tabs with Face ID or Touch ID, block ads and trackers on your device, import from Arc. No account, no telemetry. Free on iPhone, iPad and Mac (beta).

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Reji, founder of Hostao.I run several companies and dozens of websites, and for years my browser was where that work lived: one space per company, the right Gmail and Stripe already signed in. When Arc's makers said Arc stops working on 22 December, I didn't want an AI-first browser with an account. I wanted the spaces back, and less noise.So we built Tao Browser:• A space for every company, client or project. Each space has its own cookies and logins, so two Google Workspace accounts sit side by side without colliding.• Face ID / Touch ID lock for a single tab, a whole space or the app (handy when you share your screen with payroll open).• Ads and trackers blocked on the device (EasyList + EasyPrivacy).• No account, no analytics, no crash reporting. The App Store privacy label says "Data Not Collected".• On Mac: ⌘K for everything, Import from Arc, Client Mode for screen sharing, and a Wrong-Account Guard that warns you before you send from the wrong company's Gmail.It's built on Apple's WebKit, so Apple patches the engine and the Mac app is a 7 MB download. iPhone and iPad are on the App Store today; the Mac app is a free beta (the Mac App Store version is in review). Honest limits: extensions on Mac are a small reviewed set (uBlock Origin Lite, Dark Reader, Bitwarden), there's no Windows or Android build yet, and Tao isn't open source.It's free, with no ads and no in-app purchases. What would make you switch browsers for good? I'll be here all day reading every comment.

today.name: Polylane for Google Cloud

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt,I'm Ravi, co-founder of Scalekit. Today we're launching AgentKit, an MCP gateway that handles auth and tool-calling for AI agents in production.Why now? Over the last year, wiring an agent to a tool got easy. MCP standardized the interface, and any agent can now call Gmail or Salesforce after an afternoon of work.But the tool call is only the surface. Once an agent ships to real users, everything underneath it shows up:whose credentials each call executes withwhich tools each agent should have in contextthe internal systems no catalog coverswhat happens when an upstream API pushes backwho's accountable for every actionThat layer decides whether an agent makes it to production. It's what we built AgentKit for.Try it free: scalekit.com. The free tier includes 10,000 tool calls a month and all 600+ connectors. Make your first tool call from the dashboard, or start from your terminal with npx @ scalekit-inc/cli setup.Here's what it looks like in practice.Say you're shipping a sales agent inside your product. A rep types: "Prep me for the Acme renewal. Pull the deal, the last three email threads, what the team said in Slack, when we last met them, and how much they've used the product this quarter."Four apps, one ask. Getting it working for one rep in a demo is easy. Here's what's underneath when it runs for every rep at every customer:Thousands of OAuth grants, not four. 40 customers × 30 reps × Salesforce, Gmail, Slack and Calendar = 4,800 connected accounts. Each needs its tokens stored, isolated per customer, and refreshed before they expire mid-run. → AgentKit manages connected accounts end to end. Users authorize through an auth link you surface in your app. Tokens live in a per-tenant AES-256 vault, refresh automatically, and are injected at execution time. They never touch your code, logs, or prompts.Every call has to execute as the right user. The agent should see what that rep can see at that customer, and nothing more. Not a shared service account with org-wide access to every inbox. → Every tool call executes with the end user's own credentials, within the scopes they granted.Every tool definition costs context. Gmail alone exposes ~30 tools; four apps put over a hundred on the table. At ~200 tokens per definition, 40 tools burn ~8,000 tokens before the agent does any work, and tool selection gets worse as the list grows. Your prep agent needs about ten tools. Your outbound agent needs a different ten. → Virtual MCP Servers let you compose a tool set per agent role, across connectors. Each role gets one static MCP URL; you mint a short-lived session token per user per run. Smaller context and least-privilege access: ten tool definitions (~2,000 tokens) instead of over a hundred (20,000+).The data you need has no connector. Usage lives in your customer's internal analytics service. No catalog covers it, so you'd build that integration yourself, auth included. → Define it as a custom connector (OAuth 2.0, API key, bearer token, RSA or basic auth), or point AgentKit at a remote MCP server. It runs on the same gateway with the same credential handling and logs as the 600+ built-in connectors.It has to hold up and be auditable. Rate limits, timeouts, upstream errors the model can't act on. Then a deal stage changes and someone asks whether the rep did it or the agent did. → Retries and rate limits are handled on every call. Every call is logged with agent, user, tool and response, and logs stream to Datadog or Splunk.None of this shows up in a demo. All of it shows up in production. AgentKit handles that layer: 30,000+ tools across 600+ apps behind one MCP gateway. And with Triggers, an agent can start on its own the moment an email lands.Python and Node SDKs. Works with the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, LangChain, Google ADK, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, and Claude Code. You keep your framework and backend.Which of these five has slowed your agent down the most?

month.aiReview:
### ۱. مسئله و راه‌حل
بزرگ‌ترین مانع صاحبان کسب‌وکارهای کوچک (SMBs) در استفاده از ابزارهای هوش مصنوعی، نبود زمان برای تایپ پرامپت‌های طولانی و توضیح مجدد زمینه کاری در هر گفتگو است. امپیسر با اتخاذ رویکرد «صوت‌محور» (Voice-first) و ذخیره حافظه دائمی کسب‌وکار (Memory)، روند کار را به سه گام ساده تبدیل کرده است: پاسخ به ۳ سوال اولیه، ارائه دستورات صوتی، و تایید نهایی خروجی‌ها قبل از انتشار.

### ۲. معماری و تکنولوژی
معماری ابزار بر پایه تبدیل گفتار به متن (STT)، پردازش زبان طبیعی (NLP) برای استخراج نیت کاربر، و موتور مولد محتوا استوار است. حافظه زمینه‌ای (Contextual Memory) اطلاعات کسب‌وکار را حفظ می‌کند و با اتصال به بیش از ۱۰۰۰ ابزار جانبی از طریق API، وظایف عملیاتی مانند پاسخ به پیام‌ها و ایجاد اسناد را انجام می‌دهد.

### ۳. مدل درآمدی
مدل درامد ابزار مبتنی بر اشتراک نرم‌افزار به عنوان خدمت (SaaS) با دوره تست رایگان ۳ روزه است. ارائه تخفیف‌های اولیه (مانند تخفیف ۶۰ درصدی) برای جذب کاربران اولیه و تبدیل آن‌ها به مشترکان وفادار اتخاذ شده است.

### ۴. نقاط قوت
- **حذف اصطکاک ورود:** آغاز کار تنها با پاسخ به ۳ سوال و عدم نیاز به تایپ پرامپت.
- **حفظ کنترل صاحب کسب‌وکار:** گام تایید نهایی (Approval step) اعتماد کاربران را جلب می‌کند.
- **رویکرد فعالانه (Proactive):** پیش‌نویس خودکار وظایف هفته اول بدون انتظار برای درخواست کاربر.

### ۵. نقاط ضعف
- **وابستگی به اتصال اینترنت:** عدم شفافیت در عملکرد آفلاین یا ضعیف بودن شبکه.
- **چالش لهجه‌ها و کیفیت صدا:** محیط‌های شلوغ کاری ممکن است روی دقت تشخیص صوت تاثیر منفی بگذارند.
- **نیاز به الگوریتم‌های یادگیری مستمر:** مشخص نیست ویرایش‌های دستی کاربر چقدر بهینه‌سازی لحن ابزار را سرعت می‌بخشد.

در بازار ایران، فروشندگان اینستاگرامی و مشاغل محلی وقت کافی برای پاسخگویی به حجم بالای دایرکت‌ها و واتس‌اپ ندارند. نمونه ایرانی این محصول اگر بتواند تبدیل گفتار فارسی عامیانه را به خوبی انجام دهد و با سیستم‌های پیام‌رسانی بومی و پیامک یکپارچه شود، به دلیل حذف نیاز به پرامپت‌نویسی متنی، نرخ جذب (Adoption Rate) فوق‌العاده بالایی خواهد داشت.

So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
